title: Choose the visual world
question: Three dark themes have been rejected. The roll assigned The Statement of Account. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Statement of Account
options.lineage: GOV.UK Design System, HMRC self-assessment, statutory annual statements
options.thesis: Your portfolio as an official statement of account: black on white, nothing sold to you, every figure accountable.
options.viewport: A ruled sheet headed 'Statement of account'. The net result sits alone as the largest figure on the page with its own rule above and below. Positions follow as a plain ruled table, no boxes, no panels, the primary action a black bar at the top right.
options.risk: Reads bureaucratic and cold if the type is set timidly. It only works if the scale is confident and the white space generous; a literal tax-form pastiche would fail.

raised.raise: A position row and its opened trade sheet are the same structure at two scales, not a row and a separate panel.
Nothing is ever enclosed. Hierarchy comes from rules, weight and space; no card, no box, anywhere.
Hierarchy from case, indentation and one measure, never from inflating type size.
Colour encodes one law absolutely: a figure is coloured only when it is money you made or lost.

options.label: The Pink Paper
options.thesis: Your portfolio set as the day's market page on salmon newsprint.
options.viewport: A broadsheet market page. Net result as the standfirst, positions as dense ruled listings in two columns, the replay running as a boxed feature down the right.
options.risk: Also where most runs land once they leave the dark terminal, and salmon-plus-serif is the FT's house style rather than yours. Familiar and effective, but recognisably borrowed.

options.label: Deployable Sheet
options.thesis: A hand-sized packet that opens in one pull into a rigid tessellated field.
options.viewport: A compact packet that deploys into a crease field of linked cells.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a UK retail investor does not know origami engineering by heart, and a parallelogram grid fights tabular money.
options.risk: Geometry that decorates rather than encodes.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth: bitmap baselines drifting over a void, nothing ever enclosed.
options.viewport: Ivory baselines on black, the frontmost item brightest and widest.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the demoscene is not this audience's world, and amber on black is the dark terminal already rejected three times.
options.kept: Enclosure is never used; hierarchy comes from one continuous system.
options.risk: Lands back in the rejected rut wearing a different badge.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: An 80-column field on curved glass where text glows and lingers.
options.viewport: A fixed 80-column monospaced field, hierarchy from indentation and case.
options.case: Fuses poorly: this is precisely the category rut, it is monospace-only which you ruled out, and it is the third dark theme you rejected.
options.kept: Hierarchy from case and indentation, on one measure.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Rain falls according to the colour of each cloud; colour is a physical law.
options.viewport: A garden of local gravities, labels bending along each field.
options.case: Fuses badly: bending baselines over a profit-and-loss statement is a defect, and the audience identifies with none of it.
options.risk: Destroys legibility of the one thing the product exists to state.

canonCard.label: The trading terminal
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships: a dark dense terminal, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Near-black multi-pane layout, green and red everywhere, the arrangement a trader expects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other trading tool, and the direction already rejected three times here.
